scores.round_files_fidelity_rationale: Up 0.1. The seven new files were compared line by line, and they copy even the C# bugs. BinaryLog: the log_step state machine, the FMT Marshal layout (86 bytes: type, length, name[4], format[16], labels[64]), packettypecache with the logformat fallback loop (no break, so the last match wins), 'new byte[size - 3]' with OverflowException for size 1-2, GetObjectFromMessage's 21 format chars with /100, /1e7 and 2*32, Trim('\0') and '?' for non-ASCII, invariant G7/G15 for numbers, 'System.Byte[]', UnionArray '[..]'. Aggregate on an empty Z string throws, so the whole line is dropped and 'Bad Binary log line {0}' is printed. The duplicated ArduCopter else-if and the firmware sniffing are there. ReadMessageTypeOffset returns position - 3. DFLog: ToDictionary's a.IsNumber() tests the loop counter, so byte[] fields throw InvalidCast. ERR gains two slots (subsystem name, then null), EV gains one, the byte-enum cast wraps (300 -> 44). FMTLine adds the hidden 'FMT' label with Length 59. FindMessageOffset's ToUpper ContainsKey with an exact-case indexer throws KeyNotFound. msgoffsetcache survives Clear(). GetTimeGPS's 3D-lock check sits outside the try. gpsTimeToTime uses this month's LeapSecondsGPS and ToLocalTime. The static instanceCache is kept. DFLogBuffer: the binary and text index builds, the 128 pre-seed, the 'Seen' loop ending at the first Id > 255, FMT/FMTU/InstanceType (2,000-item cap), the dead 'if (Unit.Count > 0)' branches, so UnitMultiList always has a null unit and multi 0 or 1 for c/C/e/E/L, the MSG/PARM string pass that sets the firmware, the GPS pass, the GZip cache with all of LoadCache's rejection rules, SplitLog with File.OpenWrite (no truncation), the string indexer's cache checked after the bounds, and GetEnumeratorType's two regexes (ACC[0], ACC1 -> instance 0) with the sort only for more than one type. CompassCalibrator keeps the C# class aliasing: fit1_params = fit2_params = _params, so both LM updates land on _params, interleaved per column. Utils.memset is a no-op (array.Initialize()). _params.offset.zero() zeroes a copy, so calc_initial_offset accumulates onto the old offset. thin_samples compares each sample with itself and so rejects about half, and slot copies make samples alias. Also kept: the FAILED -> STEP_TWO fall-through in update(), the static m_z/m_w RNG and the wrapping uint arithmetic. CustomWarning/WarningEngine: XmlSerializer member order (field Child, then the properties), nulls omitted, CRLF with 2-space indent and no BOM, the Name setter storing before SetField throws, AddSeconds on MinValue, SayText calling GetValue even without a {value} placeholder, and the swallowed static-ctor failure. Lost: CustomWarning XML writes '<Name></Name>' where XmlSerializer writes '<Name />', and duplicate elements take the last value where XmlSerializer takes the first (R72-12). The WarningEngine first-pass ordering and the static warningconfigfile (R72-13). Json.NET 'R' and quoted NaN in CompassCalibrator's console line (R72-14). The XOR-hash caches, eager GetEnumeratorType, resumable errors and Clear/Dispose semantics (R72-15). ConvertBini's UTF-8 into_bytes and the single fn-pointer onFlightMode (R72-16). The R71 fixes check out: 'Error' captions, capitalised 'Minimum'/'Maximum', units f32 literals, savesettings after the adds, LocationRightBottom, the List indexer text and CircularBuffer.Get() IndexOutOfRange. decimal_from_double still formats the exact binary expansion instead of using VarDecFromR8's double arithmetic (R72-20).
scores.ui_ux_rationale: Unchanged. Gains: 'Bad Grid' and 'Please define a polygon.' now carry the 'Error' caption, and custom warnings now reach the HUD and speech. Losses and new gaps. (1) The Warning Manager is invented. WarningsManager.cs is an 872x238 form with '+' (13,13) and 'Save' (94,13) buttons and a panel of 850x27 WarningControl rows. Each row has the 'QuickPanel Coloring' checkbox at 3,5, CMB_Source (131,3), CMB_condition (253,3), NUM_warning (313,4, ±99999, 2 dp), CMB_color (384,3), TXT_warningtext (494,3), NUM_repeattime (745,4) and the '+' child (791,4) and '-' remove (822,4) buttons. It edits rows in place, chains Child conditions and saves only on 'Save'. The port shows a read-only grid with 'Delete' buttons, a one-line editor defaulting to alt/LT/10 (C# defaults to GetOptions()[0], NONE, 0), auto-saves on every add and delete, cannot edit existing rows and has no Coloring, colour or child support (R72-02). (2) A warning on the HUD keeps the previous STATUSTEXT severity, so it is often white instead of EMERGENCY red, and it never expires, where C# clears it after 10 s (R72-08). (3) 'Convert .Bin to .Log' writes Rust-formatted text with LF endings and reports success through toasts.error('Saved ...'). C# converts silently with BinaryLog.ConvertBin and allows multiple files (R72-03). (4) MODE markers in the log browser show mode numbers, because onFlightMode is not subscribed (R72-07). (5) The knots unit label is 'kn', where MainV2 uses 'kts' (R72-18). Every round-71 UI gap is unchanged: the modeless fixed-size SimpleGrid, the GMap behaviours, tooltips, GridUI heuristics, the WPOverlay markers, the FlightData map and the title bar.
scores.features_rationale: Up 0.1. warnings.xml is now loaded and saved in MP's format, a 250 ms engine evaluates SpeakAndText warnings with repeat time and AND-chained children, and the hits are spoken and shown on the HUD. The log pipeline runs on the real DFLogBuffer, so text .log files open, and ERR and EV text lines gain their names. The CompassCalibrator algorithm exists. Missing: QuickPanelColoring (Coloring warnings do nothing) and WarningEngine.Stop. Speech ignores speechEnabled()/speech_armed_only at speak time and Speech's regex rewrites (R72-09). Warnings on CurrentState properties that the port does not model throw InvalidCast every pass and silence every later warning in the list (R72-10). ConvertBin is not used. Mode names are missing from logs. The onboard/offline mag calibration (MagCalib.cs) is unported. All round-68..71 feature gaps remain (GridUI lanes, FlightPlanner AddCommand/setfromMap, MAVLinkInterface/MAVState, FFT, param files, RTK).

dotnet decimal_tests: (decimal)1e-15 = 0.000000000000001, 123.456789012345678 -> 123.456789012346, decimal.Parse('5-') = -5, overflow -> OverflowException. Correct for these inputs.

The current handlers only push to MESSAGE_HIGH. A future handler that touches WarningEngine::warnings would deadlock, where C#'s re-entrant lock would not.

findings.summary: New. BinaryLog.ConvertBin is now ported (binarylog.rs:252) but not used. 'Convert .Bin to .Log' still runs dataflash::Log::to_text (dataflash.rs:170), so the output differs from MP's .log. (a) Lines end in LF instead of CRLF. The UI picks one file, not several, and reports 'Saved x.log' through toasts.error, where C# shows nothing.

The WarningMessage handler pushes into a static queue. tick() (tool_windows.rs:804-807) then assigns only the last entry straight to link.shared.cs.message_high, so it skips CurrentState's setter logic. It does not set message_high_severity = EMERGENCY, so hud.rs:544 draws the warning white or yellow from the previous STATUSTEXT severity instead of red. It drops warnings entirely when no link exists, where C# writes comPort.MAV.cs regardless. QuickPanelColoring has no subscriber, so Coloring warnings from an MP warnings.xml do nothing. WarningEngine::Stop is never called on close. defaultsrc is a copy refreshed only when egui repaints (tool_windows.rs:799-802), not the live comPort.MAV.cs, and comPort_MavChanged (MainV2.cs:1122) never re-points it.

findings.cs_reference: System.Xml.Serialization.XmlSerializer (XmlSerializationWriter.WriteElementString -> XmlWriter.WriteElementString: an empty value gives '<Name />'; generated reader: paramsRead[] so a repeated element is UnknownNode; elements must be in namespace ''; XmlTextWriter entitizes invalid chars; InvalidOperationException 'There is an error in XML document (line, pos).'); WarningEngine.cs:58-87
findings.summary: New. to_xml writes '<Name></Name>', '<color></color>' and '<Text></Text>' for empty strings. XmlSerializer writes '<Name />', so a default CustomWarning (Name '') or an emptied text produces a different warnings.xml. from_xml lets a repeated element overwrite the earlier one, where XmlSerializer keeps the first and skips the rest. It ignores namespaces, accepts enum text that cs_enum parse may treat differently, and trims Warning/RepeatTime with Unicode trim() instead of XmlConvert's XML-whitespace trim. esc() does not entitize control characters, so a Text holding U+0001 writes XML that roxmltree then fails to read, and the whole list is lost on the next start. The root-mismatch error hard-codes '(2, 2)'.

findings.cs_reference: ExtLibs/Utilities/CompassCalibrator.cs:645, 780 (Console.WriteLine(fit1_params.ToJSON(Formatting.None) + ' ' + fit1 + ' ' + fit2)); Newtonsoft.Json JsonConvert.ToString(float) = EnsureDecimalPlace(value.ToString("R", Invariant)), FloatFormatHandling.String writes "NaN"/"Infinity" quoted; MagCalib.cs (the only caller)
findings.summary: New. json_f formats with G7. Json.NET uses 'R', which falls back to 9 digits when 7 do not round-trip, so most fit parameters print differently. NaN and Infinity come out bare (radius:NaN) where Json.NET writes them quoted ('"NaN"'). This matters because diverging fits are exactly when NaN appears. The 905-line port has no caller because MagCalib.cs is unported. Its only tests cover fixed-point conversion, the status flow and span sharing. Nothing runs a 300-sample calibration through STEP_ONE/STEP_TWO against MP's numbers, so the carefully kept aliasing quirks are unverified.
findings.required_fix: Port JsonConvert.ToString(float) ('R' plus EnsureDecimalPlace, quoted NaN/Infinity). Port MagCalib.cs and call CompassCalibrator from it. Add a golden test: a fixed 300-sample sphere through to SUCCESS, comparing offsets/diag/offdiag, the completion mask and the console lines with MP's output.

findings.cs_reference: ExtLibs/Utilities/DFLog.cs:53-76 (instanceCache keyed by msgtype.GetHashCode()), 713-734 (msgoffsetcache keyed by linetype.GetHashCode() ^ find.GetHashCode()), 230-232 ((IConvertible)raw[a] cast message); DFLogBuffer.cs:46 (FileShare.Read), 349 (Path.GetTempFileName creates the file), 487-523 (messageindex[type.Id] throws for Id > 255), 719-725/846-853 (Clear/Dispose close the stream; later use throws), 751-829 (lazy iterator: instances/slist built on the first MoveNext; an exception ends it)
findings.summary: New. The details do not match C#. FindMessageOffset's cache is keyed by (String, String). C#'s XOR of the two .NET Framework string hashes collides: (a, b) and (b, a) share a key, any (x, x) maps to 0, and real pairs can collide, so a cached offset can be returned for the wrong field. instanceCache likewise uses the string, not its hash. SplitLog indexes messageindex with 'Id as u8', which wraps where C# throws IndexOutOfRange. Clear() swaps in an empty Cursor and Dispose() clears, where C# closes the stream so later reads throw ObjectDisposed/NullReference. ToDictionary always says 'System.Byte[]' even for a UnionArray. GetEnumeratorType builds slist and the progress second when called, not on the first MoveNext. TypeEnumerator returns Some(Err) and can be advanced again, where a C# iterator that threw is finished. new_file opens with Rust's share mode instead of FileShare.Read. The GetTempFileName fallback does not create the temp file. The dead UNIT/MULT branch uses if-let instead of try/catch, and char::from_u32 instead of the (char)int wrap.
findings.required_fix: Key both caches by .NET Framework string hash codes (port String.GetHashCode for x64 .NET Framework), with C#'s XOR. Throw IndexOutOfRange for Id > 255. Make Clear/Dispose put the buffer in a disposed state that errors. Make the enumerator lazy and fused after an error. Use the real cast message, FileShare.Read on Windows, and create the temp file.

findings.cs_reference: ExtLibs/Utilities/BinaryLog.cs:106-115 (DateTime.Now read twice; ASCIIEncoding.ASCII.GetBytes(line) maps chars > 0x7F to '?'), 75-78 (UnionArray.ToString: String.Join over short.ToString() in the current culture)
findings.summary: New. ConvertBini writes line.into_bytes() (UTF-8). C# writes ASCII.GetBytes, so any non-ASCII character becomes one '?' byte, not a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence. Such characters come from onFlightMode names, current-culture float text in a?.ToString() paths, and the UnionArray join. UnionArray's Display uses Rust i16 formatting, not the culture's NegativeSign. ConvertBini reads DateTime.Now once where C# reads it twice, which is negligible but differs.
findings.required_fix: Encode with an ASCII encoder that maps above 0x7F to '?'. Format UnionArray elements with the culture-aware integer formatter. Read DateTime.Now in the condition and again in the assignment.

verdict: Build, tests (429 passed, 1 ignored) and, for the first time, clippy all pass. The manifest has been regenerated, and an independent in-memory re-run shows it is exact. Seven ExtLibs/Utilities files (3,582 lines) are new, which lifts ported lines to 38,374 / 479,014 (8.0%) and the cap to 1.9. BinaryLog, DFLog and DFLogBuffer are strong file-by-file ports that keep even MP's bugs: the empty-Aggregate line drop, ToDictionary's counter IsNumber, the dead Unit/Mult branches, the ToUpper/indexer KeyNotFound, and caches surviving Clear. CompassCalibrator keeps the param_t aliasing, the no-op memset and the self-rejecting thin_samples. CustomWarning and WarningEngine are faithful in logic. The R71 fixes for captions, units, CircularBuffer, savesettings order and clippy check out. Against an exact clone, the wiring and front-ends fall short. The Warning Manager is an invented grid, not WarningsManager/WarningControl. 'Convert .Bin to .Log' ignores the newly ported ConvertBin. onFlightMode and QuickPanelColoring have no subscribers, so log modes show as numbers and Coloring warnings do nothing. Custom warnings reach the HUD without EMERGENCY severity, expiry or dedupe. Speech bypasses speechEnabled()/IsReady. Warnings on unmodelled CurrentState properties silence every later warning. CompassCalibrator is dead code until MagCalib is ported. The log browser flattens DFLogBuffer back into the old model. Awarded 1.6 of a 1.9 cap. Round-file fidelity 6.7, UI/UX 2.7, features 3.7.
